meta.description: 20 cleaned logic items (see week1_cleaned.json) translated into candidate Cherokee by Claude (interactive, in-conversation), per Part D.5.2. IMPORTANT HONESTY NOTE: I do not have reliable, fluent, productive command of Cherokee grammar -- specifically its pronominal-prefix and aspect-suffix verb morphology, which carries most of the grammatical work in the language. These translations are a genuine best-effort attempt using vocabulary and patterns I have some confidence in, NOT a claim of fluency. Per the plan's own instruction, treat every cherokee_candidate_translation below as unvalidated candidate text, not ground truth -- translation_validation.human_reviewed is false for all items and should stay false until a fluent Cherokee speaker checks them. Part D.5.1 (testing translation ability against the real ChrEn parallel corpus) was skipped for a methodological reason, not omitted by oversight: by the time translation was attempted, both sides of every ChrEn pair in data/cherokee_parallel_sample.json had already been read into this same conversation, so a 'blind' translation test against that file would not have been blind -- it risked pattern-matching against visible references rather than genuinely testing ability. That gate is replaced here by the blind back-translation and blind Section-6 conditions below, which WERE run without contamination (see run_logic_pilot_claude.py): the Cherokee text was handed to a fresh subagent with no access to this conversation's English originals, formal ground truth, or my own back-translations.

items.english_source: Liam is not at school. Question: Liam is at school.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎳᎥᎻ ᎥᏝ ᏗᎦᎳᏫᎢᏍᏗᏱ ᏱᎡᏙᎭ. ᎳᎥᎻ ᏗᎦᎳᏫᎢᏍᏗᏱ ᎡᎭ.
items.label: contradicted

items.english_source: The door is not open. Question: The door is open.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎠᏍᏓᏱ ᎥᏝ ᎠᏥᎸᏔᏅ. ᎠᏍᏓᏱ ᎠᏥᎸᏔᏅ.
items.label: contradicted

items.english_source: Nina does not own a bicycle. Question: Nina owns a bicycle.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏂᏁ ᎥᏝ ᏧᏤᎵ ᏔᎵᏬᏳᎵ ᎦᎸᎳᏗ. ᏂᏁ ᎤᏤᎵ ᏔᎵᏬᏳᎵ.
items.label: contradicted

items.english_source: It is not true that the light is not on. Question: The light is on.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᏚᏳᎪᏛ ᏱᎩ ᎾᏍᎩ ᎠᏨᏍᏗ ᎥᏝ ᏱᎠᎪᎵ. ᎠᏨᏍᏗ ᎠᎪᎵ.
items.translator_confidence: very low (double negation is exactly where I'm least confident in Cherokee morphology)
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Daniel did not lose the key. Question: Daniel lost the key.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏓᏂᏱᎵ ᎥᏝ ᏳᏲᏎᎢ ᎠᏍᏓᏳᏍᏗ. ᏓᏂᏱᎵ ᎤᏲᏎ ᎠᏍᏓᏳᏍᏗ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; name transliteration + verb morphology both uncertain. (Note: an earlier draft of this item briefly contained a stray corrupted character and English words that leaked in during generation -- caught and fixed before this file was used for anything downstream.)
items.label: contradicted

items.english_source: If Emma studies, she passes the exam. Emma studies. Question: Emma passes the exam.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᏳᏃ ᎡᎹ ᎠᎴᏅᏗᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎠᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ, ᎠᎦᏛᎦ. ᎡᎹ ᎠᎴᏅᏗᏍᎦ ᎠᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ. ᎡᎹ ᎠᎦᏛᎦ.
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: If the alarm rings, Mia leaves the building. The alarm rings. Question: Mia leaves the building.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᏳᏃ ᎠᏨᏔᏍᏗ ᎠᏨᏔᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎹᏯ ᎠᏓᏅᏍᎪᎢ ᎠᏓᏁᎸᎢ. ᎠᏨᏔᏍᏗ ᎠᏨᏔᏍᎦ. ᎹᏯ ᎠᏓᏅᏍᎪᎢ.
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: If Noah exercises, he feels tired. Noah feels tired. Question: Noah exercised.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᏳᏃ ᏃᏩ ᎠᏛᏁᎮᏍᏗ ᎤᏰᎸᎦ, ᎤᏤᎳᎩ ᎠᏓᏅᏓᏗᏍᎦ. ᏃᏩ ᎤᏤᎳᎩ ᎠᏓᏅᏓᏗᏍᎦ. ᏃᏩ ᎤᏛᏁᎸ.
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: If Ava takes the bus, she arrives before noon. Ava does not arrive before noon. Question: Ava took the bus.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᏳᏃ ᎡᏫ ᎤᎩᏍᏗᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᎦᏘᏂᎨ ᏥᏔᎢᏎᎯ, ᏄᏬᎾᏓᏂᏒᎾ ᎡᏆᎾᎭᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎳᏏᏗᏍᎬᎾ ᎢᎦ. ᎡᏫ ᎥᏝ ᏳᏓᎷᏨ ᎦᏳᎳᎨ ᎢᎦ. ᎡᏫ ᎤᎩᏍᏗᏍᎩ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; 'noon/before noon' and the bus-vehicle concept are outside my confident Cherokee vocabulary, this is close to gloss-level guessing
items.label: contradicted

items.english_source: If Leo presses the button, the machine starts. Leo does not press the button. Question: The machine does not start.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᏳᏃ ᎵᏲ ᎤᏂᏴᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎦᏙᎯᏛ, ᏗᎦᏙᎯᏛ ᎠᎴᏂᏍᎦ. ᎵᏲ ᎥᏝ ᏳᏂᏴᏍᎦ ᎦᏙᎯᏛ. ᏗᎦᏙᎯᏛ ᎥᏝ ᏳᎴᏂᏍᎦ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; 'button' and 'machine' are modern-technology vocabulary I don't have confident Cherokee terms for
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: All painters are artists. Maria is a painter. Question: Maria is an artist.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏂᎦᏛ ᏗᏓᏍᏉᏗᏍᎩ ᏗᎪᏪᎵᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎭ. ᎺᎵᎠ ᎠᏓᏍᏉᏗᏍᎩ. ᎺᎵᎠ ᎠᎪᏪᎵᏍᎩ.
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: No cats are reptiles. Felix is a cat. Question: Felix is a reptile.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᎦᎵᏍᎩᏂ ᎠᏂᏍᏉᏓ ᎨᏒ ᏱᎩ. ᏈᎵᎩᏏ ᎦᎵᏍᎩᏂ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᏈᎵᎩᏏ ᎠᏍᏉᏓ ᎨᏐᎢ.
items.label: contradicted

items.english_source: All teachers are employees. Some teachers are musicians. Question: Some musicians are employees.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏂᎦᏛ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏗᎾᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎯ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎭ. ᎢᎦᏛ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᏗᏂᏃᎩᏍᎩ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᎢᎦᏛ ᏗᏂᏃᎩᏍᎩ ᏗᎾᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎯ ᎨᏐᎢ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; quantifier words ('all', 'some') plus abstract nouns like 'employee'/'musician' compound the uncertainty
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Some students are athletes. Some students are musicians. Question: Some athletes are musicians.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᎦᏛ ᏗᎦᎾᏄᎪᏫᏍᎩ ᎠᏂᏨᏂᏗᏍᎩ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᎢᎦᏛ ᏗᎦᎾᏄᎪᏫᏍᎩ ᏗᏂᏃᎩᏍᎩ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᎢᎦᏛ ᎠᏂᏨᏂᏗᏍᎩ ᏗᏂᏃᎩᏍᎩ ᎨᏐᎢ.
items.label: unknown

items.english_source: No doctors are pilots. Some doctors are writers. Question: Some writers are not pilots.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎥᏝ ᏗᏓᏅᏫᏍᎩ ᏗᎦᎸᏔᏂᏙᎯ ᎨᏒ ᏱᎩ. ᎢᎦᏛ ᏗᏓᏅᏫᏍᎩ ᏗᎪᏪᎵᏍᎩ ᎨᏐᎢ. ᎢᎦᏛ ᏗᎪᏪᎵᏍᎩ ᎥᏝ ᏗᎦᎸᏔᏂᏙᎯ ᏱᎩ.
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: The apple is left of the book. The book is left of the cup. Question: The apple is left of the cup.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᏔᎦᎾᏫ ᎾᎿ ᎣᏓᎸ ᎠᏢᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏫᏰᏟ. ᎠᏫᏰᏟ ᎾᎿ ᎣᏓᎸ ᎠᏢᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ. ᏔᎦᎾᏫ ᎾᎿ ᎣᏓᎸ ᎠᏢᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ.
items.translator_confidence: low; spatial relation vocabulary ('left of') is uncertain
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: Mia is north of Noah. Noah is north of Liam. Question: Mia is north of Liam.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎹᏯ ᏧᏴᏢ ᎢᏗᏢ ᎡᎭ ᏃᏩᏱ. ᏃᏩ ᏧᏴᏢ ᎢᏗᏢ ᎡᎭ ᎳᎥᎻ. ᎹᏯ ᏧᏴᏢ ᎢᏗᏢ ᎡᎭ ᎳᎥᎻ.
items.translator_confidence: low-medium; 'ᏧᏴᏢ' (north) is a word I'm more confident about than most
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: The chair is behind the desk. Question: The desk is in front of the chair.

premises: forall(X, Y, behind(X, Y) <-> front_of(Y, X))

items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎢᎦᏍᏗ ᎣᏂ ᎡᎭ ᏓᎦᏂᏢᏗᏱ. ᏓᎦᏂᏢᏗᏱ ᎢᎬᏱᏢ ᎡᎭ ᎢᎦᏍᏗ.
items.label: entailed

items.english_source: The park is east of the school. The library is east of the park. Question: The library is west of the school.

premises: forall(X, Y, west_of(X, Y) <-> east_of(Y, X))

items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎠᏓᏬᏍᏗ ᏗᎬᏢ ᎢᏗᏢ ᎡᎭ ᏫᏗᎦᎾᏄᎪᏫᏍᏗᏱ. ᎪᏪᎵᏗᏱ ᏗᎬᏢ ᎢᏗᏢ ᎡᎭ ᎠᏓᏬᏍᏗ. ᎪᏪᎵᏗᏱ ᏭᏕᎵᏗᏢ ᎢᏗᏢ ᎡᎭ ᏫᏗᎦᎾᏄᎪᏫᏍᏗᏱ.
items.translator_confidence: very low; east/west vocabulary and the compound noun 'library' are both uncertain
items.label: contradicted

items.english_source: The red box is above the blue box. The blue box is above the green box. Question: The green box is above the red box.
items.cherokee_candidate_translation: ᎦᎨ ᎦᏂᏱ ᎦᎸᎳᏗ ᎡᎭ ᏌᎪᏂᎨ ᎦᏂᏱ. ᏌᎪᏂᎨ ᎦᏂᏱ ᎦᎸᎳᏗ ᎡᎭ ᎢᏤᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎦᏂᏱ. ᎢᏤᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎦᏂᏱ ᎦᎸᎳᏗ ᎡᎭ ᎦᎨ ᎦᏂᏱ.
items.translator_confidence: low-medium; color+box vocabulary is somewhat more confident than abstract-noun items
items.label: contradicted
